items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The row's self-declared primary warrant (device_notes: the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7; strongest_rejected_alternative: 'the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6') fails at byte tier. Prov.19.7 spliced from verse_map_oshb.json is כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה - fourteen whitespace tokens including the inline ketiv/qere pair לא לוֹ at words 12-13 - opening on the quantifier כָּ֥ל at word 1, with the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6 and the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ; the particle therefore relates the verse's own first clause, כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ (words 1-4), to its second, מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ (words 7-9), and no particle opens the verse, so the cross-seam grammatical dependency the row rests on is byte-false and, by the row's own words, load-bearing: high under the severity law, exactly as filed. Testing the row against the finding: the residual friend-root is real but does not bind the pair at token tier. Word-bound consonantal-skeleton sweeps (whitespace-token equality, verse counts) give 19:6's הָ֝רֵ֗עַ (skeleton הרע) 2 of 915 verses (Prov.17.17, Prov.19.6) and 19:7's מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ (skeleton מרעהו) 3 of 915 (Prov.12.26, Prov.19.4, Prov.19.7), disjoint sets, and the skeleton token sets of Prov.19.6 and Prov.19.7 intersect in the empty set even with function words counted. The exact-token catchwords around the row are hubbed on the non-adjacent Prov.19.4, ה֗וֹן יֹ֭סִיף רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝דָ֗ל מֵרֵ֥עהוּ יִפָּרֵֽד: 19:4 shares מרעהו with 19:7 (3 of 915) and רבים with 19:6 (רַ֭בִּים at 19:6 word 1, רַבִּ֑ים at 19:4 word 4; word-bound 7 of 915), while the intervening Prov.19.5 shares no skeleton token with 19:4, 19:6 or 19:7, so no contiguous cluster can be built on that chain either. Root-level adjacency is too common to carry a cluster on its own: at accent-stripped tier the friend-noun family (tokens containing resh with tsere followed by ayin, the object that excludes the patach-pointed evil homograph) occurs in 37 of 915 verses with 6 adjacent-verse pairs book-wide (Prov.14.20-14.21, 17.17-17.18, 19.6-19.7, 25.8-25.9, 25.17-25.18, 27.9-27.10), and the row itself declines to rest on it. OW-3 both sides, all three seams weighed under C2's ruled default (single_proverb; proverb_cluster only on byte-grounded cohesion named in the rationale): leading seam, the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.5, עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט, against the row's opening verse Prov.19.6, רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי נָדִ֑יב וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן, no shared skeleton token; trailing seam, the row's closing verse Prov.19.7 against the following row's opening verse Prov.19.8, קֹֽנֶה לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא טֽוֹב, no shared skeleton token; the row-internal seam 19:6|19:7 carries no shared token either, only the cognate friend-noun in different forms and different slots (19:6's in its second colon, words 5-8, וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן, after the etnahta on word 4, נָדִ֑יב; 19:7's at word 7 in its first colon), which is theme-plus-cognate glue, the over-clustering the strategy says the mesh will challenge. Parashah layer: no PE or SAMEKH at Prov.19.5-19.8 in pmarks_Prov.json (the nearest PE is at Prov.19.9; single-witness, tier-3, absence never counterevidence). Span ruling endorse_proposal, with qualification: the atomization to Prov.19.6-Prov.19.6 and Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7 (both single_proverb, parent C2 unchanged) is byte-sound because it is the collection default reasserting itself once the only load-bearing warrant falls and no replacement byte object binds 19:6 to 19:7 more tightly than each binds to 19:4; every digit in the proposal re-verifies (pmarks_Prov.json records 1 ketiv/qere note and 1 paseq seg at Prov.19.7, single-witness, the paseq layer count-only; מרעהו 3 of 915; הרע 2 of 915), and it remains a proposal for owner triage - nothing is applied. A rival re-warranting of the pair on the cognate friend-noun plus the antithetic gift-giver/poor-man frame would be possible only at low confidence and would have to pass the test that killed the original, which the token-tier evidence above does not let it do. Ruled coherently with M8-Prov-289#p38-2, the positional item on the same internal seam: that repair is byte-true and transfers to the proposed Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7 row as its own internal-device statement, so the two items do not conflict.

Re-derived from bytes. Prov.19.7, כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה, carries the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ, so under the verse's own accentuation the second half opens on word 10, מְרַדֵּ֖ף, and the friend-form מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ stands at word 7 inside the first half; under the alternative tricolon reading the second colon opens on the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6, again not on the friend-form. The rationale's clause that 19:7 'opens its second colon with' that form is therefore byte-false on both readings, exactly as filed, and medium is right: the clause is a defective positional warrant claim, not alone load-bearing, since the row's stated force rests on the dependency claim adjudicated at M8-Prov-289#p38-1. The mark disclosures in the same sentence re-check against pmarks_Prov.json: 1 ketiv/qere note at Prov.19.7 (the inline pair לא לוֹ at words 12-13) and 1 paseq seg at Prov.19.7, both cited single-witness, the paseq claim verse-level only, which is all the count-only inventory can source; the row's WEB quotes “everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts” (web:Prov.19.6) and “his friends avoid him” (web:Prov.19.7) are verbatim substrings of the staged WEB verses. The proposed repair is validated as a proposal: the replacement placement (word 7, inside the first half, etnahta on word 9) and the replacement wording for strongest_rejected_alternative (the a-fortiori pair at words 5-6 governing 19:7's own two clauses rather than the seam) are byte-true on the verse itself and need no source beyond it. OW-3 both sides, weighed from bytes: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.5, עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט, shares no skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.19.6, רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי נָדִ֑יב וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן; the row's closing verse Prov.19.7 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.19.8, קֹֽנֶה לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא טֽוֹב; the internal 19:6|19:7 seam shares none, and the friend-forms' true slots (19:6 word 6 in the second colon after the etnahta on word 4; 19:7 word 7 in the first colon before the etnahta on word 9) show the two occurrences are not even colon-symmetric, so the corrected placement removes rather than supplies cluster support. Ruled coherently with M8-Prov-289#p38-1: because that item's atomization proposal is endorsed, this repair applies to the proposed Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7 row's internal-device statement if the owner adopts the respan, or to the shipped row if the span is left standing; the corrected wording is the same bytes either way.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. Prov.19.13, הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה, is eight words with the etnahta on word 4, כְּסִ֑יל, so the wife-noun אִשָּֽׁה at word 8 is colon-final and verse-final; Prov.19.14, בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת, is seven words with the etnahta on word 4, אָב֑וֹת, so אִשָּׁ֥ה at word 6 is colon-medial, followed by מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת. The observed_substrate_signals entry 'exact repeated noun at the same line-final slot' is therefore byte-false on the slot and contradicts the row's own boundary_rationale, which places the noun verse-final in 19:13 and colon-medial in 19:14; 'exact' is also a tier overclaim, since the two forms differ at byte tier and at accent-stripped tier (accent stripping retains the meteg that 19:13's form carries: an accent-stripped substring sweep of 19:13's form hits 1 of 915, Prov.19.13 alone, while 19:14's unmarked form hits 10 of 915 excluding Prov.19.13) and coincide only at consonantal-skeleton tier, אשה. Filed severity medium is right: the entry is a defective warrant statement in the dependent evidence field, not alone load-bearing, because the warrant survives on independent bytes re-swept here - the skeleton token אשה word-bound (whitespace-token equality, verse counts) returns 9 of 915 verses (Prov.6.26, 6.32, 7.10, 11.22, 18.22, 19.13, 19.14, 30.20, 31.30) and Prov.19.13-19.14 is the only adjacent pair among them (the contiguous-substring sweep, sweep.py --skel, is wider at 11 of 915, adding Prov.2.16 and Prov.7.5 through prefixed forms, and still yields the same single adjacent pair); the father-root the rationale argues is byte-true in both first cola, לְ֭אָבִיו at 19:13 word 2 and אָב֑וֹת at 19:14 word 4, the etnahta word itself, but is absent from observed_substrate_signals. The proposed repair (rewrite the first entry to name the skeleton tier and the true slots; add the father-root entry) is validated as a proposal: every element is byte-true and its digits are the ones above; confidence high survives on the exclusive adjacency and the paired frame. OW-3 both sides, weighed from bytes: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.12, נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ, shares no skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.19.13; the row's closing verse Prov.19.14 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.19.15, עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב; no PE or SAMEKH at Prov.19.12-19.15 in pmarks_Prov.json, and no ketiv/qere or paseq at either verse of the span. Both edges hold and the only live cohesion object sits inside the row, where it decides for the pair.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. Prov.20.5, מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה, is eight words with the etnahta on word 5, which is the bare man-noun itself, אִ֑ישׁ; Prov.20.6, רָב אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא, is nine words with the etnahta on word 5, חַסְדּ֑וֹ, the bare man-noun standing at word 4, אִ֣ישׁ. The rationale's clause that the bare noun 'stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both (word 5 of 8 in 20:5, word 5 of 9 in 20:6)' is byte-false on either reading of its parenthetical - as the noun's position, 'word 5 of 9' is wrong at 20:6 (word 4); as the etnahta's position, the digits are right but 'ahead of the etnahta in both' is wrong at 20:5, where the noun carries it - while device_notes states the byte-true asymmetry, so the row contradicts itself, exactly as filed. Medium is right: the defective clause sits inside the warrant description, but the warrant itself survives on independent bytes re-swept here - verses carrying both the bare token איש and the waw-prefixed token ואיש word-bound (whitespace-token equality, consonantal skeleton) are exactly 2 of 915, Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6; the bare token word-bound is 53 of 915; the contiguous-substring sweep of the same consonants (sweep.py --skel) is 87 of 915, matching the row's three digits; and the waw-prefixed instance does open the second colon in construct with an abstract quality noun in both, וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה at 20:5 words 6-7 and וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים at 20:6 words 6-7. The observed_substrate_signals etnahta entry is byte-true as written. The proposed repair (re-cut the parenthetical to the device_notes reading: etnahta-bearing at 20:5 word 5 of 8, one word ahead of the etnahta-bearing word at 20:6 word 4 of 9) is validated as a proposal on the bytes above. OW-3 both sides, weighed from bytes: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.20.4, מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ ישאל וְשָׁאַ֖ל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן (1 ketiv/qere note in pmarks_Prov.json, the inline pair ישאל וְשָׁאַ֖ל at words 5-6, single-witness), shares no skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.20.5; the row's closing verse Prov.20.6 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.20.7, מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו; no PE or SAMEKH at Prov.20.4-20.7, no ketiv/qere or paseq at 20:5 or 20:6. Both edges hold, the row's rejection of extension either way stands on bytes, and the exclusive same-verse doubling decides for the cluster.

Re-derived from bytes and both witnesses (the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so mood is argued from pointed bytes plus renderings, never asserted as machine-verified). Prov.23.24, גול גִּ֣יל יגול יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק יולד וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם וישמח יִשְׂמַח בּֽוֹ (4 ketiv/qere notes in pmarks_Prov.json, matching the four inline pairs the row names, cited single-witness), carries the qere verb יָ֭גִיל at word 4, preceded by the qere infinitive absolute גִּ֣יל at word 2, and the qere יִשְׂמַח at word 11; Prov.23.25, יִֽשְׂמַח אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ, opens on יִֽשְׂמַח and closes its second colon with וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל. device_notes labels both 23:24's יָ֭גִיל and 23:25's יִֽשְׂמַח third-person jussive wishes; for 23:24 that contradicts the row's own boundary_rationale (which reads 23:24 as the general maxim and 23:25 as its applied wish) and the second witness, which renders 23:24 indicative, “The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.” (web:Prov.23.24), and only 23:25 as a wish, “Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!” (web:Prov.23.25). The bytes corroborate the finding independently of the rendering: 23:24's verb is the long imperfect form of its root, whereas Proverbs itself attests the shortened form of the same root where a wish or prohibition is meant, אַל יָגֵ֥ל at Prov.24.17 words 7-8 and וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל at Prov.23.25 word 4, and accent-stripped substring sweeps keep them apart (the accent-stripped form of 23:24's verb hits 2 of 915, Prov.2.14 in a plural and Prov.23.24; the accent-stripped form of 24:17's short verb hits 1 of 915; the accent-stripped form of 23:25's short verb hits 1 of 915), while the infinitive-absolute-plus-imperfect construction of 23:24 is the assertive intensifier, not a wish. Qualification: a volitive sense of a long-form imperfect is not impossible in poetry, so the replacement claim is 'indicative on both witnesses' readings and by form', not a machine-verified label; 23:25's יִֽשְׂמַח is form-ambiguous for its root, but its parallel short form settles the wish reading there. Medium is right: the mislabel is the stated ground of the mandated unit_type deviation disclosure - a defective warrant claim - but not load-bearing, because the deviation conclusion survives on the shared absence of a governing second-person imperative or vetitive in either verse (none of 23:24's twelve tokens or 23:25's five is one). The proposed repair (split the mood claim; rest the disclosure on that shared absence) is validated as a proposal on the bytes above. OW-3 both sides, weighed from bytes: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.23.23, אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה, shares no skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.23.24 (only the cognate wisdom root, חָכְמָ֖ה against חָ֝כָ֗ם, word-bound חכם 26 of 915); the row's closing verse Prov.23.25 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.23.26, תְּנָֽה בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תרצנה תִּצֹּֽרְנָה; the row-internal seam is bound by the word-bound skeleton token ישמח (11 of 915 verses, Prov.23.24-23.25 one of only two adjacent pairs, the other Prov.29.2-29.3), and the mood shift the repair names (long indicative form at 23:24, short jussive form at 23:25) is exactly the maxim-to-wish turn across that seam that the rationale argues, so the corrected disclosure strengthens rather than weakens the pair. Ruled coherently with M8-Prov-405#p38-2 on the same row: neither item changes the span.

Re-derived from bytes both ways. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative tests only the atomization rival (24 alone, 25 separate); no field tests the extension rival, and a byte-visible device does straddle the row's leading seam. The second-person father-and-mother pair stands at Prov.23.22, שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ (לְ֭אָבִיךָ word 2, אִמֶּֽךָ word 9), and at the row's own closing verse Prov.23.25, יִֽשְׂמַח אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ (אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ words 2-3); contiguous-skeleton sweeps (sweep.py --skel, verse counts) give the father-form 5 of 915 (Prov.1.8, 6.20, 23.22, 23.25, 27.10) and the mother-form 4 of 915 (Prov.1.8, 6.20, 23.22, 23.25), so 23:22 and 23:25 are two of only four verses book-wide carrying the pair, and the begetting root runs יְלָדֶ֑ךָ (23:22 word 4), וְיוֹלֵ֥ד (23:24 word 8, qere) and יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ (23:25 word 5) under spelling variation (contiguous ילד 3 of 915: Prov.17.21, 23.22, 27.1; contiguous יולד 4 of 915: Prov.17.17, 17.25, 23.24, 23.25), with the father-noun also at 23:24 word 5, אֲבִ֣י. That is an inclusio-shaped frame over Prov.23.22-23.25 which neither this row nor the embedded neighbours name; under the cross-seam cohesion rule an undisclosed byte-true device straddling the row's seam argues continuity against the row, so the finding is real, and medium is right rather than high because the shipped span remains byte-defensible: the row's own seam catchword is the tighter object (the word-bound skeleton token ישמח closing 23:24's qere at word 11 and opening 23:25, 11 of 915 verses with Prov.23.24-23.25 one of only two adjacent pairs), and the intervening Prov.23.23, אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה, carries its own governing imperative-plus-vetitive frame (קְ֭נֵה word 2, וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר words 3-4) and shares no skeleton token with 23:22 beyond the function word ואל, nor any with 23:24 beyond the cognate wisdom root (word-bound חכם 26 of 915). The frame is a contiguous-skeleton object, not a word-bound one: the skeleton token sets of Prov.23.22 and Prov.23.25 intersect in the empty set because the forms differ by prefix, so the auditor's tier naming is exact.
